alternativeSelection.assessment: Two qualified substantial responses retained; each37.5ECsociology plus distinct methods or political/environmental application. No dedicated demography/family/migration sequence or third coherent distinct sociology response can be assembled merely by relabelling adjacent psychology/law. Three is a maximum, not target.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Both introduce sociological perspectives on social institutions and relationships.
Both develop sociological questions and ways of interpreting social phenomena.

Inequality is substantial in the UCR sociology core, especially Social Movements & Environmental Justice, placed with the more specific climate/inequality component. Its credits are not duplicated here; the broad required stratification course remains separately visible.
Both develop contemporary sociological theory; UCR includes different theorists and themes.
Both connect culture/media to social difference; UCR centres racial representation.
No retained course centres sociological/demographic family formation, fertility, household task division and their quantitative analysis. Lifespan psychology has a different primary object.
Both address life-course change, with UCR approaching it through developmental psychology.

Radboud centres macro-micro-macro explanations, bridging assumptions and testable mechanisms. The selected UCR social theories are relevant but do not establish that specific analytical toolkit as a primary subject.
Both teach social inquiry, with UCR focused on qualitative methods.
Descriptive statistics are taught within BENGATE102, whose integrated research project is placed with Leerproject1. No second use of that UCR course is counted here.

Both integrate research questions, measurement, data collection, analysis and group reporting, including survey research. Radboud specifies a9EC sociological project with face-to-face structured interviews; UCR combines a substantial empirical project with general methods/statistics.
Both teach inferential quantitative analysis of social/behavioural data.
UCR offers philosophy courses but no single scheduled component equivalent to this social-science philosophy requirement.

HCBPSYC211 includes factor analysis, PCA and scale reliability, but its primary inferential-statistics relationship is already represented with Toetsende statistiek. This separate3EC social-measurement component is not counted again.
Both teach regression analysis; UCR econometrics uses economic and social datasets.

No remaining scheduled UCR course primarily implements this second cumulative sociology survey project integrating the linked inference, scale-construction and regression courses. Real UCR empirical projects remain acknowledged without duplicating those course credits.

Radboud integrates survey-data analysis with conducting/analyzing focus groups in a sequential mixed-methods project. UCR offers genuine quantitative and qualitative research, but no selected course establishes this integrated design/project as its primary subject.

Required individual sociology research applies theory, scale construction and regression to existing data and presents a thesis. Optional UCR independent research is displayed separately from the scheduled180EC and is not guaranteed equivalent work.
The Radboud course centres criminological explanations, empirical tests and crime-prevention policy. Broad socio-legal foundations and conflict studies do not establish this primary subject.
Both examine group relations and social influence; UCR approaches these psychologically.
Both examine how evidence relates to public policy; UCR focuses on public economics.
No closely comparable retained UCR component; public debate and sociological skills remain a distinct requirement.
Both involve academic and personal development in distinct curricular settings.
Professional and personal development remains a distinct Radboud course.

Both examine democratic backsliding, populism and political/social change through comparative analysis. Radboud centres modernization/postmodernization and backlash theory; UCR compares political systems and institutions. This is stronger than general EU institutional study.

Both directly connect inequality and environmental questions through social theory and justice. UCR centres environmental-justice movements and case studies; Radboud applies sociological inequality frameworks to climate behaviour and a creative project.
This unrestricted 6-EC course is student-selected; no fixed UCR equivalent is imposed.
Third-year Radboud professional development is a separate credited requirement.
Genuine 12-EC free space remains open to student choice.
The compulsory 13-EC labour-market internship has no same credited UCR placement.

notes.text: Both UCR programmes sustain sociology and empirical social inquiry, with complementary psychology, law, economics and political or environmental study. UCR includes survey/data work and qualitative projects; the closest match also develops measurement, statistical modelling and evidence synthesis. Radboud integrates these skills through a denser sociology sequence, successive supervised survey projects, dedicated mixed methods, a compulsory 13 EC internship and a 9 EC sociology thesis. These curricular relationships do not establish degree equivalence or credit transfer.

audience.programmeDescription: Sociology at Radboud studies inequality, social relationships and conflict. It integrates sociological theory, quantitative social research, policy questions, families and life courses through successive empirical projects, an internship and a thesis.
audience.comparisonExplanation: Both UCR programmes contain 37.5 EC of sociology courses, including qualitative research, alongside general methods, statistics and an empirical team project. The closest match adds statistical modelling, measurement, evidence synthesis and developmental perspectives. The second connects sociology to political change, climate communication and sustainability governance. Radboud offers a more concentrated sequence in family and life-course sociology, cumulative survey research and mixed-methods integration, with a required internship and thesis.

curriculum.routeLabel: Ordinary bachelor; Political Change and Opposition plus Climate Change and Inequality
curriculum.limitation: The complete 180 EC contains 150 EC of compulsory study, 12 EC of restricted sociology choices and 18 EC of open electives. The two displayed choices are permitted examples; Diversities in Care is an alternative, inseparable 5+1 EC pair. RADAr-NL is mandatory without credit. Second-year entry requires 42 EC of Year 1; compulsory Year 3 requires all of Year 1. Internship entry requires 90 compulsory EC, including all of Year 1 and a pass in Leerproject 2 or Leefstijlen, plus career training before the placement. Methods and thesis progression conditions apply. This annual framework does not guarantee future offerings. UCR does not confer this degree, a professional qualification or automatic master admission.
